Subject: BlueWave kickoff recap — context-window playbook (post-call)

Jessica — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed immediate next steps so we have a shared plan going into the eval:

- What we heard (you confirmed): BlueWave needs high-fidelity document summarization and structured extraction across patient case records and regulatory attachments. Typical documents are long (10–40k tokens) and include embedded tables and scanned PDF text.
- Primary concerns you raised: truncation and hallucination in long summaries, consistent patient-identifiers handling, and predictable token cost for budgeting.
- What Redwood will deliver for the first phase (30-day scoped):
  1) A context-window playbook — recommended model variants, quantization and batching knobs for your throughput profile.
  2) A small benchmark set and baseline metrics for summarization fidelity, truncation breakdowns, and cost per 1k tokens.
  3) Prompt set + eval harness (we'll run on your sample and share results).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Jessica: please confirm the drive folder we can use for sample docs (we have the one you shared in the call but need write access).
- BlueWave procurement: please loop in any contracting constraints (C14 export controls, minimum term) if relevant.
- Aditya / Marcus: prepare a short technical playbook and two model recommendations (low-latency and high-quality) + attach an initial benchmark CSV and prompt-set draft by Monday EOD.

Attachments: context-benchmarks.csv (baseline metrics stub), prompt-sets-v1.jsonl (example prompts), MAPS-Model-Recs.pdf (high-level model tradeoffs) — all referenced in the drive link below.

I'll set a 30-min follow-up next Wednesday to review initial results. Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Thanks Kimberly — jumping in with the technical plan and suggested model choices. High-level notes first, then links and files.

Summary of technical risks & mitigations
- Truncation risk: long documents with relevant late-context (e.g., signed summaries at the end) cause information loss. Mitigation: chunk+overlap strategy with hierarchical summarization (document -> section summaries -> final synthesis) and KV-cache-aware prefix caching for repeated patient headers.
- Hallucination risk in synthesis: minimize via extract-then-verify pipeline (NER + rule-based checks) and conservative decoding (lower temperature + logit bias).
- Cost predictability: recommend quantized variants for batch offline jobs and mixed-precision (int8 on dedicated) for interactive routes.

Model recommendations (pilot):
1) Redwood-XL-16k-qa (high-quality): best overall summary fidelity on our long-doc benchmarks; higher token cost, lower throughput.
2) Redwood-Medium-32k-optimized (latency/cost): a trimmed-parameter variant with KV cache optimization; slightly lower ROUGE but 2–3x throughput improvement.

Benchmark links and artifacts
- Benchmarks CSV (attached): per-doc ROUGE/LCS, truncation events, tokens per request, latency (p95).
- Prompt set: prompt-sets-v1.jsonl contains 45 seed prompts for extraction, section summarization, and final synthesis.
- Public baseline: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/long-context/bluewave-report (fast view).

Sample prompts (excerpts)
- "Extract all patient identifiers and list them with source page numbers."
- "Summarize the clinical findings in 3 bullet points, preserving timeline order."
- "Provide a one-paragraph synthesis suitable for an insurance pre-authorization review."

Operational notes
- We recommend starting with a 2,000–4,000 token chunk size and 10–15% overlap for scanned/ocr-heavy docs, then iterating.
- For production, use a rolling cache keyed by patient_id+doc_hash to reduce repeated preface costs.

Attachments included in the drive link. Happy to pair on a test run Mon/Tue.

— Aditya

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of clarity we needed. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

1) Truncation scenarios: can you quantify how often we should expect truncation on a 32k-token model versus the 16k option given our doc mix? A ballpark % of documents that would need overlap/chunking would help our product budget planning.
2) Cost question: for the initial 30-day pilot (approx. 15,000 pages, mixed OCR) — which model would you run to balance cost and fidelity? Can you give us a pilot estimate (monthly cost range) we can use for procurement?
3) Data residency / logs: procurement wants to know retention window for inference traces and whether logs that include sample text are exportable for audits.

Also, can you add a simple decision tree in the playbook: when to pick hierarchical synth vs single-pass summarization (we expect some documents are short enough to avoid chunking)?

If we can get a one-page decision tree + pilot cost range and an initial run of 100 documents by Tuesday, procurement will be comfortable moving to a short SOW.

Jessica — thanks, good questions. Short answers and concrete next steps below. I'll drop the one-page decision tree and a pilot cost estimate into the Drive folder and schedule the 100-doc run.

Quick answers
- Truncation frequency: based on our internal sampling for similar mixes, a 32k model reduces overlap/chunking needs by ~65% vs 16k on long OCR-heavy docs. Expect ~20–25% of your files to require chunking with 32k, versus ~55–60% with 16k (ballpark; we'll quantify on your samples).
- Pilot cost (15k pages, mixed OCR):
  • Using Redwood-XL-16k-qa (pilot run, higher quality): estimated $9k–12k for the 30-day run (higher CPU/OCR preprocessing + retries).
  • Using Redwood-Medium-32k-optimized (cost-focused): estimated $5k–7k for the same run (faster throughput, lower per-token unit cost).
- Data residency / logs: Redwood retains inference traces by default for 30 days; export for audit is available as CSV (PII redaction options configurable). For Private deployments we can extend retention policies.

Action items (who / when)
- Aditya: run initial 100-doc pass (mixed OCR set) and upload metrics CSV + summary into Drive — target Tue EOD (2026-08-11).
- Aditya / Marcus: add one-page decision tree to MAPS-Model-Recs.pdf and update model-recs slide with cost ranges — Tue EOD.
- Kimberly: I will open a short SOW draft and confirm procurement contacts; cc'd procurement when we have the cost numbers.

Scheduling: I'll propose two 30-min slots for Wed/Thu to review the 100-doc results.

Attachments (uploaded to drive): context-benchmarks.csv, prompt-sets-v1.jsonl, MAPS-Model-Recs.pdf

Thanks — this feels like a clean, actionable plan.
